speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an infant experiencing recurrent stridor and wheezing; please note that while infants cannot speak, I will be observing your breathing patterns and may need to speak to your parents or guardians to clarify details. To begin, during which specific activities do these episodes of stridor and wheezing occur?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia. The combination of stridor and wheezing exacerbated by crying, feeding, and neck flexion, along with post-prandial vomiting, is classic for this condition. Given the recurrent nature and potential for feeding difficulties, I am requesting an upper airway evaluation. REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_Flexion_Photos_and_Videofluoroscopy.
